name: Matthew Nielsen
tagline: I build tools and apps that handle the tedious parts for you: browser automation, scrapers, local-first desktop apps, and lately Android apps and games.
about: I'm a software engineer and Colorado School of Mines computer science graduate (Robotics & Intelligent Systems). I build things I actually want to use, and I keep at them until they work end to end.

Most of that work is on my GitHub: Pilot, a Python agent that drives a real browser with Playwright and records successful runs so it can replay them without calling a model; LinkWatch, an Electron app that watches pages for new links on a schedule; SacredSafe, an offline password manager with AES-256 encryption; Weekly Schedule, a native Android planner built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose; and Protect Your Plot, a lane-defense game I'm building in Godot for Android.

Across all of it I lean toward local-first software: tools that run on your own machine, need no account and keep your data with you. My coursework is up there too, from a Java Clue game with computer players to route-finding search algorithms in Python.
I write a short blog post about what I work on each day, so you can see how the projects come together.
